title: Portulacaria
wikitext:
{{Short description|Genus of succulent plants}} {{Automatic taxobox | image = Jade leaves.jpg | image_caption = ''Portulacaria afra'' | image2 = 1 Portulacaria afra - Spekboom South Africa.jpg | image2_caption = Mature Portulacaria afra | parent_authority = | taxon = Portulacaria | authority = [[Nikolaus Joseph von Jacquin|Jacq.]] | subdivision_ranks = Species | subdivision = }} '''''Portulacaria''''' is a [[genus]] of [[succulent plant]], classified in its own subfamily '''Portulacarioideae''' in the family [[Didiereaceae]]. It is indigenous to [[southern Africa]]. ==Taxonomy== The genus was previously placed in the family [[Portulacaceae]], but according to molecular studies is part of [[Didiereaceae]]. It has further been revised when phylogenetic tests showed conclusively that genus ''Ceraria'' was located within ''Portulacaria'', and all ''Ceraria'' species have consequently been renamed and moved into this genus.P.Bruyns, M.Oliveira-Neto, G.F. Melo de Pinna, C.Klak: ''Phylogenetic relationships in the Didiereaceae with special reference to subfamily Portulacarioideae''. Taxon 63 (5). October 2014. 1053-1064. ===Species=== [[File:Ceraria pygmaea 01.jpg|thumb|right|''[[Portulacaria pygmaea]]'' (formerly Ceraria pygmaea)]] {{As of|2024|March}}, [[Plants of the World Online]] accepted the following species:{{Cite POWO|title=''Portulacaria'' Jacq..|id=32713-1|access-date=2024-03-17|mode=cs1}} *''[[Portulacaria afra]]'' Jacq. *''[[Portulacaria armiana]]'' van Jaarsv. *''[[Portulacaria carrissoana]]'' (Exell & Mendonça) Bruyns & Klak, syn. ''Ceraria pygmaea'' Pillans ==Uses== ''[[Portulacaria afra]]'' normally uses [[C3 carbon fixation|{{c3}}]] (or Hatch-Slack) carbon fixation but is also able to switch to [[Crassulacean acid metabolism|CAM]] carbon fixation when drought stressed. It is a local delicacy and its leaves are eaten by the local peoples. It is also popular internationally as a garden plant.{{cite journal |doi=10.1104/pp.85.2.481 |title=Physiological Changes in Portulacaria afra (L.) Jacq. during a Summer Drought and Rewatering |year=1987 |last1=Guralnick |first1=L. J. |last2=Ting |first2=I.
